Lawyer here. Not trying to keep myself in a job but we work in legalese for a reason, not just to keep ourselves in jobs.

See, words are tricky things. A statement that makes perfect sense to you and means one thing may quite easily mean something different to someone else. Lawyers are particularly good at making words mean something else. When we draft contracts and statutes we do so knowing that at some point another lawyer is going to try and make it mean something other than what we want it to mean in order to benefit their client. So we add more words to make absolutely clear what we mean and to rule out any exceptions or twists in the language. Of course the result of that is that we end up with a bunch of rules and exceptions to rules and then exceptions to exceptions and only we can read it. But when we do read it, it means what we wanted it to say and not what some Smartass lawyer thinks we wanted it to say.

My law: change the structure of the government.

The problem with the United States is that the authors of the constitution did not anticipate problems with population growth. There are now too few people making decisions for too many others. It makes bribery easy for special interest groups and corporations and it makes it hard for citizens to hold politicians responsible for their actions.

But the solution isn't for government to grow sideways. Nobody would be served if there were tens of thousands of representatives in Washington. Instead, the government needs to expand vertically. We need another federal layer so that individual governments can be small again and respond to the will of the people.

1. No more than 50,000 people per state/territory

The smallest currently is Northern Mariana Islands with about 54,000 people so every one would be split at least once.

The smallest state, Wyoming, for example, would have to split into at least 12 states. The largest, California would split into at least 777.

2: No more than 50 states/territories per region

Regions are geographic areas smaller than the country but larger than a state.

Max population = 50,000 x 50 = 2.5 million, the population of the United States when it declared independence

With the current population of the United States, there would be at least 128 regions

A major city and its surrounding area could become a single region split into multiple states.

States can vote to leave one region and join another

3. New federal structure

Citizens of states elect state representatives

Citizens of states elect regional representatives to represent their state in the regional government

Citizens of states elect national representatives to represent their state and their region in the national government

Citizens of states elect state senators

State senators elect regional senators

Regional senators elect national senators

(The 17th Amendment was a mistake)

State governors, regional governors, and the president are elected by popular vote

(No electoral college)

Circuit court system is replaced by regional courts

4. Powers

The national congress has very few powers like the founders intended (currency, war, etc.)

The powers that come from a liberal interpretation of the necessary and proper clause and the commerce clause now belong to regional congresses.

The natural result of this system will be that governments are closer to the will of the people.

Liberal regions will have liberal laws, conservative regions will have conservative laws, libertarian regions will have libertarian laws, and there will be a spectrum of regions in between.

The national government will make sure they cooperate with each other but will no longer try to impose one way of life on the whole country.

States would be smaller but retain the powers they currently have and would prevent regional governments from centralizing power

TLDR:

Federal -> State -> Local

becomes

National -> Regional -> State -> Local
